summary: This bill increases Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits by requiring them to be calculated using a "low-cost food plan" instead of the current "thrifty food plan," establishes a standard medical expense deduction for elderly or disabled SNAP recipients, removes the cap on excess shelter expenses, and eliminates the time limit for able-bodied adults without dependents to receive SNAP benefits.

scores.thoughts: This bill would increase government spending by expanding eligibility and increasing benefit levels for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). The shift from the 'thrifty food plan' to the 'low-cost food plan' and the changes to deductions would lead to higher outlays.

The bill directly expands the social safety net by increasing SNAP benefits, making it easier for eligible individuals to receive assistance, and eliminating time limits for certain recipients. These changes aim to reduce food insecurity and provide more support to low-income households.

The bill's core provisions replace the thrifty food plan with the higher-cost low-cost food plan for calculating SNAP benefits, expand medical and shelter deductions, and eliminate the ABAWD time limit. These changes directly increase federal mandatory spending on SNAP with no revenue offsets or cuts elsewhere, making the legislation primarily an expansion of entitlement spending.
